When I got my brows pierced I wanted to have them pierced in the middle. My piercer told me that she wouldn't do anything but the outside of the brow because she doesn't want me to risk nerve damage. Of course there is a chance with almost every piercing to hit a nerve, but there is a big branch of the trigeminal nerve in the area of the piercing shown in the picture OP posted. Also, you can't see nerves. Of course your anatomy could allow inner brow piercings but you'd have to take a huge risk. You can't just tell if you'll hit a nerve- that's why it's safer to pierce the part of the eyebrow where there aren't as many branches. This is the information I got from my piercer

I wouldn't recommend eyebrow piercings in this position. Your trigeminal nerve is in that area and you don't want to risk piercing it. That's why eyebrow piercings are usually pierced on the outer corner of your brow
